summary: This is a web application where users can search for a lunar landing site and time window to help them determine if the landing site is ideal. The azimuth angle for the sun and earth are used to determine if they are visible from the lunar landing site. The website features a 2d or 3d map for users to select a location on the moon, and the program provides a landing site assessment. It provides multiple map views for an intuitive understanding as well as tiled images of the sected site to visualize the terrain from DEM information and spot observations. Sites are graded out of 10, based on the terrain visibility, solar elevation angle, sunlight duration, and direct access to earth. It gives a summary of site in relation to the sun to assess power generation potential and to the earth to ensure maximum direct-to-Earth communication windows and minimize satellite relays. The website also allows you to compare two landing sites with different time windows, and to compare to previous lunar landing sites from NASA databaases. It pulls from lunar site databases to provide a map overlay or the most likely sites on the south pole as has been selected as candidates from the Artemis 3 missions. It provides this a map overlay, including sites from other regions.
details:
• The website takes coordinates and a time window as input, and outputs a landing site assessment for the user
  • The landing site assessment is a quick and simple way to see whether the site is viable based on the terrain visibility, solar elevation angle, sunlight duration and direct access to earth
  • The UI allows users to choose points on a 2d or 3d map of the moon, and previous landing sites (like the Apollo missions) are included as points of interest for reference or comparison
  • The lunar topography feature shows an image of the moon's surface at the given coordinate, and data relating to the elevation, slope, and roughness
  • The comparison feature of the site allows users to compare two location with two different time windows (or it can be used on the same location at two different time windows, or different locations in the same time window)
  • The Ephemeris results plot the sun and earth sky positions with the terrain horizon from the perspective of the landing site, allowing users to easily visualize the visibility of the sun and earth for power and communication requirements
